column1: # Curated IRD (inherited retinal disease) phenotype terms → HPO, for upstream-agent phenotype
# inference (NO human-in-the-loop). The orchestrator maps a study's described symptoms / disease
# names to these HPO terms and passes them to Exomiser; if nothing matches, the default root term
# HP:0000556 (Retinal dystrophy) is used so a run never blocks on phenotype.
# This table is the ALIAS layer over the full HPO index (hpo_lexicon.tsv.gz): it exists for clinical
# shorthand the ontology has no name for — DISEASE names used as phenotype shorthand ("Stargardt") and
# field abbreviations ("LCA", "BBS"). An exact ontology name always wins over a row here (see
# mapper.map_phrase), so rows do NOT need to restate terms HPO already names.
# All HPO IDs verified against the HPO API (ontology.jax.org) 2026-07-12; rows added 2026-07-15 were
# verified against the bundled HPO 2026-06-23 lexicon. Expand as needed — keep keywords specific
# (matching is word-boundary anchored, so short aliases like "ird" cannot fire inside another word).
# NOTE a disease-name alias maps to the phenotype the diagnosis directly asserts, and no further: "BBS"
# yields Retinal dystrophy, not the syndrome's obesity/polydactyly/renal features. Those are real BBS
# features but are NOT stated by the text, and inventing findings a clinician did not write is how a
# phenotype-driven differential quietly becomes fiction. LIRICAL's own HPO/OMIM annotations supply what
# the disease implies; our job is only to encode what was said.
